predecessors.name: Achaemenid Empire
predecessors.text: Phoenicia and Cyprus, which 'declared their independence from Persian rule' soon after the failed Egyptian campaign of about 351

successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: Phoenicia (Sidon burnt, Tennes put to death in 346-345) and Cyprus ('In 343 BC, Artaxerxes committed responsibility for the suppression of the Cyprian rebels to Idrieus')

ledger.x: 350 BCE: Phoenicia rises against Artaxerxes III under Tennes of Sidon.
350 BCE: Phoenicia is free of Persian rule.
350 BCE: the revolt begins; 'Artaxerxes personally led an army of 330,000 men against Sidon'.
346 BCE: Sidon falls and Phoenicia is retaken.
343 BCE: the last rebel ground is taken.
343 BCE: the revolt is over; the land returns to the Achaemenid Empire.

wars.name: Revolt of Phoenicia and Cyprus against Artaxerxes III
wars.outcome: Sidon was burnt and Tennes put to death (346-345); Idrieus of Caria was given the Cyprus campaign in 343 and reduced the island.

certainty.note: No page gives the rebels' frontiers; the Phoenicia and Cyprus regions stand in.
